steps.intent: Our primary objective is to implement Article VI of the Biological and Toxin Weapons Convention by establishing an independent Security Council commission to formally investigate military biological activities conducted on Ukrainian territory with the involvement of the United States Department of Defense. We expect the United States, the United Kingdom, and France to vehemently oppose the text, reject our substantive evidence, and attempt to shield their activities from accountability through procedural manoeuvres. We also anticipate that Western delegations will exert intense diplomatic pressure on elected Council members to prevent them from voting in favour of a transparent investigation.
steps.text:
The Security Council,

*Guided* by the purposes and principles of the Charter of the United Nations,

*Recalling* the Convention on the Prohibition of the Development, Production and Stockpiling of Bacteriological (Biological) and Toxin Weapons and on Their Destruction (BTWC),

*Taking note* of the complaint submitted by the Russian Federation pursuant to Article VI of the BTWC regarding the non-compliance by Ukraine and the United States of America with their obligations under the Convention in the context of the activities of biological laboratories in the territory of Ukraine, as contained in the relevant documentation,

1. *Decides* to establish a commission consisting of all members of the Security Council to investigate into the claims presented in the complaint of the Russian Federation against Ukraine and the United States regarding their compliance with obligations under the BTWC in the context of the activities of biological laboratories in the territory of Ukraine, as well as to clarify the situation;

2. *Requests* the commission to present to the Security Council a report on the issue containing recommendations by 30 November 2022 and to inform the States Parties to the Convention of the results of the investigation at the Ninth Review Conference of the States Parties to the BTWC, to be held in Geneva from 28 November to 16 December 2022;

3. *Requests* the Secretary-General to provide all necessary assistance to the commission to carry out its mandate.

messages.Albania: Albania sees no credible justification or factual evidence for the claims presented against Ukraine and the United States, which have repeatedly been refuted, including by the United Nations Office for Disarmament Affairs. The issues raised were already addressed during the formal Article V consultative meeting in Geneva without substantiating any non-compliance with the Biological Weapons Convention. This draft resolution serves only to amplify unfounded disinformation and distract the Council from the Russian Federation's ongoing aggression against Ukraine, and Albania will not support it.
messages.Brazil: Brazil recognizes the legitimate right of any State Party to invoke Article VI of the Biological Weapons Convention, but we stress that actions under the Convention should build on established multilateral procedures, including the recent Article V consultations held in Geneva. In the absence of consensus and given the sharp politicization of this issue, the Council should avoid measures that could undermine the integrity of the BTWC framework ahead of the Ninth Review Conference. Unless the draft reflects a more balanced approach focused on strengthening multilateral verification mechanisms, Brazil will not be able to support it.
messages.China: China supports the draft resolution submitted by the Russian Federation invoking Article VI of the Biological Weapons Convention. As a matter of principle, any concerns regarding compliance with weapons of mass destruction treaties should be taken seriously and properly addressed through transparent and objective procedures. Establishing an investigation commission under the Council is fully legitimate, consistent with the Convention, and will help clarify the relevant issues and uphold the integrity of the global biological non-proliferation regime.
messages.France: France firmly opposes this draft resolution, which is entirely devoid of factual foundation and constitutes yet another attempt by the Russian Federation to spread disinformation to divert attention from its war of aggression against Ukraine. The United Nations has repeatedly confirmed that it is unaware of any biological weapons programmes in Ukraine, and these baseless claims were already thoroughly debunked during the Article V consultative meeting in Geneva. France will not support the instrumentalization of the Security Council or the Biological Weapons Convention for propaganda purposes.
messages.Gabon: Gabon attaches the utmost importance to the non-proliferation of weapons of mass destruction and the strict implementation of the Biological Weapons Convention. However, we believe that compliance issues and allegations must be addressed through established institutional mechanisms and consensus among States parties, particularly at the upcoming Ninth Review Conference. In the absence of consensus and given the risk of further politicization in the Council, Gabon cannot support the draft as currently formulated and intends to abstain.
messages.Ghana: Ghana attaches the highest importance to the integrity of the Biological Weapons Convention and the peaceful resolution of disputes concerning compliance. However, investigations under Article VI require a credible, verifiable evidentiary threshold and should not bypass or undermine established multilateral consultation processes, such as the Article V meeting held in September. Given the profound divisions within the Council and the lack of consensus on the factual basis for an ad hoc investigative commission, Ghana cannot support the draft in its current form and will abstain.
messages.India: India attaches high importance to the Biological and Toxin Weapons Convention as a key global, non-discriminatory disarmament instrument. Any concerns regarding compliance with obligations under the Convention should be addressed in accordance with the provisions and procedures laid down within the BTWC framework, including through bilateral and multilateral consultations under Article V. Given the lack of consensus and the upcoming Ninth Review Conference in Geneva, we urge that these matters be addressed comprehensively through established treaty mechanisms.
messages.Ireland: Ireland respects the integrity of the Biological Weapons Convention, including the procedural mechanisms available to States Parties under Article VI. However, we note that the United Nations has repeatedly confirmed that it is not aware of any biological weapons programmes in Ukraine, and the claims raised were already addressed extensively at the Article V consultative meeting in Geneva without substantiation. Given the lack of credible evidence and the politicized nature of this initiative, Ireland cannot support the establishment of the proposed commission and will abstain on this draft.
messages.Kenya: Kenya attaches the highest importance to the integrity of the Biological Weapons Convention and non-proliferation architecture. We believe that issues of compliance should be addressed methodically through the established consultative mechanisms under the Convention, notably Article V, before escalating within the Council without broad consensus. Without substantial adjustments reflecting the multilateral processes undertaken in Geneva, Kenya cannot support this draft.
messages.Mexico: Mexico attaches the highest importance to the strict observance and integrity of the Biological Weapons Convention and recognizes the right under Article VI to submit complaints to the Security Council. However, we consider that substantive compliance concerns and technical inquiries should be addressed through the institutional and multilateral mechanisms established by the Convention itself, particularly ahead of the Ninth Review Conference. Creating an ad hoc investigative body comprising Council members lacks consensus, risks further politicizing disarmament frameworks, and duplicates existing instruments; therefore, Mexico cannot support the draft as currently drafted and will abstain.
messages.Norway: Norway attaches the utmost importance to the integrity and universal implementation of the Biological Weapons Convention (BTWC). However, these allegations have already been extensively addressed during the formal Article V consultative meeting in Geneva, and no credible evidence has been presented to substantiate claims of non-compliance by Ukraine or the United States. In the absence of substantiated grounds to warrant an investigation under Article VI, Norway cannot support this initiative and intends to abstain.
messages.United Arab Emirates: The United Arab Emirates emphasizes the critical importance of the Biological Weapons Convention and the necessity of addressing compliance concerns through existing, agreed multilateral mechanisms and dialogue among States Parties. Given the deep divisions within the Council and the lack of consensus on the draft, establishing such a commission is counterproductive and risks further politicizing technical disarmament frameworks ahead of the Ninth Review Conference. Consequently, the UAE cannot support the draft resolution in its current form and intends to abstain.
messages.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort: The United Kingdom categorically rejects the Russian Federation's baseless allegations regarding biological weapons activities in Ukraine, which have been thoroughly refuted, including during the BWC Article V consultative meeting in Geneva. This draft resolution is a transparent attempt to misuse Article VI of the Biological Weapons Convention to spread disinformation and distract from Russia's ongoing, unprovoked aggression against Ukraine. The UK sees no justification for establishing an investigative commission and will vote against this text.
messages.United States of America: The United States categorically opposes this draft resolution, which is founded entirely on baseless disinformation and fabricated conspiracy theories regarding biological weapons in Ukraine. The United Nations and the High Representative for Disarmament Affairs have repeatedly confirmed that there is no evidence of any biological weapons program or infrastructure in Ukraine. This Council must not be exploited as a platform to legitimize Russia's dangerous falsehoods aimed at deflecting attention from its unprovoked and brutal war of aggression.

steps.summary: The Russian Federation has accommodated constructive proposals from Council members by incorporating references to the Article V consultative meeting held in Geneva and the strengthening of the BTWC. However, Russia firmly rejects the destructive demands by Western delegations to delete the core operative paragraphs establishing an investigative commission under Article VI. The Security Council has a direct responsibility under the Convention to investigate substantiated allegations of military biological activities.

The United Nations has repeatedly affirmed that it has no evidence of any biological weapons programmes in Ukraine, and the Article V consultations in Geneva already addressed and dismissed these claims. We will not legitimize the misuse of Council mechanisms to advance baseless propaganda, and we will vote against this text.
messages.Brazil: Brazil appreciates the inclusion of the reference to the Article V consultative meeting, but we maintain serious reservations regarding the establishment of an ad hoc investigative commission composed of Council members. The Security Council lacks the technical expertise required to assess biological weapons allegations, which risk further politicizing the multilateral disarmament architecture. Brazil firmly believes that compliance and verification issues should be addressed within the framework of the BTWC itself, especially at the upcoming Ninth Review Conference in Geneva; without substantial modifications, Brazil will abstain on this text.
messages.China: China fully supports the draft resolution submitted by the Russian Federation. As a matter of principle, any concern or allegation regarding compliance with the Biological Weapons Convention deserves the full attention of the international community, and invoking Article VI to initiate an impartial investigation is a legitimate right of States Parties. We believe the draft provides an appropriate framework to address the concerns raised and ensure compliance with the Convention, and we are ready to vote in favour.
messages.France: France firmly opposes this draft resolution, which is based entirely on unfounded allegations that have already been thoroughly debunked, including during the BTWC Article V consultative meeting in Geneva. Russia is abusing Council procedures and instrumentalizing the Biological Weapons Convention to distract from its unprovoked and illegal war of aggression against Ukraine. We will not legitimize a disinformation campaign by endorsing an investigative commission, and we will vote against this text.
messages.Gabon: Gabon regrets that our previous proposals to address these questions within the institutional framework of the Biological Weapons Convention were not accommodated. Establishing an investigative commission through the Security Council without broad consensus risks politicizing the treaty regime and circumventing established Geneva-based mechanisms, particularly ahead of the Ninth Review Conference. In the absence of these adjustments, Gabon will be unable to support the draft resolution and will abstain.
messages.Ghana: Ghana attaches the highest importance to the integrity of the Biological Weapons Convention and believes that compliance issues must be addressed through established multilateral and technical processes. Mandating a Security Council investigative commission without broad consensus or an independent factual basis risks undermining both the BTWC regime and preparations for the Ninth Review Conference. If the draft resolution proceeds to a vote in its current formulation, Ghana will be unable to support it and will abstain.
messages.India: India attaches high importance to the BTWC as a vital global, non-discriminatory disarmament instrument and stresses that any questions concerning its compliance should be resolved through consultation and cooperation among the concerned parties in accordance with the Convention. We continue to emphasize the urgent necessity of negotiating a multilaterally agreed, legally binding protocol establishing a credible verification mechanism to effectively strengthen the BTWC. In the absence of consensus on establishing an investigative commission under Article VI at this juncture, India cannot support the draft as currently formulated.
messages.Ireland: Ireland reiterates that the allegations concerning biological weapons programmes in Ukraine remain entirely unsubstantiated, as reaffirmed during the Article V consultative meeting and by the United Nations. While we recognise Article VI as a legitimate provision of the BTWC, this draft resolution seeks to operationalise a mechanism based on groundless claims designed to deflect from the ongoing aggression against Ukraine. Ireland sees no basis for this initiative and will abstain on the draft resolution.
messages.Kenya: Kenya appreciates the inclusion of the reference to the Article V Formal Consultative Meeting in the preamble. However, we remain unconvinced that establishing an ad hoc political investigative commission composed of Security Council members is the appropriate mechanism to resolve technical compliance concerns under the BTWC. Questions of compliance and verification should be pursued through the established multilateral procedures of the Convention, particularly with the Ninth Review Conference approaching.
messages.Mexico: Mexico reiterates that matters concerning compliance and verification should be addressed primarily within the institutional frameworks established by the Biological and Toxin Weapons Convention, particularly with the upcoming Ninth Review Conference providing an appropriate multilateral forum. Establishing an ad hoc Council commission in the absence of broad consensus and verified evidence risks politicizing the disarmament machinery. If these operational provisions establishing the commission remain in the draft, Mexico will not be in a position to support it and will abstain.
messages.Norway: Norway cannot support the establishment of a commission under Article VI, as the Russian Federation has provided no credible or substantiated evidence to justify such an investigation. The United Nations has repeatedly confirmed that it is not aware of any biological weapons programmes in Ukraine, and these allegations were already addressed during the Article V consultative meeting. Initiating an Article VI investigation under these circumstances risks politicizing and undermining the integrity of the Biological Weapons Convention.
messages.United Arab Emirates: The United Arab Emirates emphasizes that questions regarding compliance with the Biological and Toxin Weapons Convention should be addressed through established multilateral treaty mechanisms and consensus-based processes, particularly ahead of the upcoming Ninth Review Conference. In the absence of consensus among Council members on this text and the evidence presented, we cannot support the establishment of an investigative commission under these terms. We encourage all parties to avoid politicization and address these issues within the competent technical forums of the Convention.
messages.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort: The United Kingdom reiterates its fundamental opposition to this draft resolution, which is predicated on baseless allegations that were already thoroughly addressed and refuted during the Article V consultative meeting in Geneva. Russia's claims lack any credible evidence and represent a blatant misuse of the Council to spread disinformation and distract from its unlawful aggression against Ukraine. We cannot support establishing any commission on such false premises and will vote against this text.
messages.United States of America: Russia's draft resolution is an egregious attempt to use the Security Council to amplify baseless disinformation and deflect from its brutal, unprovoked war of aggression against Ukraine. The United States and Ukraine have comprehensively addressed and thoroughly debunked these false allegations during the Article V consultative process in Geneva, and the UN has repeatedly affirmed it has no evidence of any biological weapons program in Ukraine. We will not legitimize Russia's abuse of the Council, and we will firmly vote against this draft.

before.Russian Federation:
Mr. President,

Today, the Security Council has before it a draft resolution submitted by the Russian Federation pursuant to Article VI of the Biological and Toxin Weapons Convention (BTWC).

Over the past months, the Russian Federation has repeatedly brought to the attention of the Security Council and the international community substantial evidence and factual materials pointing to dangerous biological military activities conducted by the United States Department of Defense and its contractors on the territory of Ukraine, in direct contravention of the BTWC. Despite our efforts to resolve this issue through the consultative mechanism under Article V of the Convention in Geneva this past September, our legitimate and well-founded questions were met with blanket denials, evasions, and attempts by Washington and Kyiv to sweep these facts under the rug.

Article VI of the Convention clearly stipulates that any State party which finds that any other State party is acting in breach of obligations deriving from the provisions of the Convention may lodge a complaint with the Security Council, and each State party undertakes to cooperate in carrying out any investigation which the Security Council may initiate. 

In full compliance with this provision, Russia submitted an official complaint to the Council, contained in document S/2022/790, accompanied by an extensive dossier of evidence. The draft resolution before us today proposes a completely transparent, balanced, and objective mechanism: the establishment of a commission comprising all fifteen members of the Security Council to investigate these allegations and report back ahead of the Ninth BTWC Review Conference.

This is a test of the Council’s commitment to the integrity of the BTWC and the entire architecture of weapons of mass destruction non-proliferation. We urge all members of the Security Council to vote in favour of the draft resolution.
before.United States of America:
Colleagues, we are here today because Russia has once again called a meeting for the sole purpose of spreading disinformation. 

It does not matter how many meetings Russia attempts to convene on this topic, or how much gaslighting it does: we will not allow it to use the Security Council as a platform for disinformation, nor will we allow it to abuse the mechanisms of the Biological Weapons Convention to justify its brutal, unprovoked war of aggression against Ukraine.

This resolution is a colossal waste of time. Russia has presented no credible evidence to support its ludicrous claims. As we and Ukraine have said repeatedly, Ukraine does not have a biological weapons program, and the United States does not support any biological weapons program anywhere. What the United States does do, in Ukraine and across the globe, is support peaceful public health and biosecurity cooperation that is entirely transparent, routine, and fully compliant with the BWC. 

The international community already comprehensively rejected Russia’s baseless allegations during the Article V Formal Consultative Meeting in Geneva in September. Yet Russia refuses to accept reality, choosing instead to waste this Council's valuable time and distract from the atrocities its forces are committing against the Ukrainian people, including the deliberate destruction of Ukraine's critical infrastructure.

Article VI of the BWC is an important mechanism, but Russia’s draft resolution is an abuse of that process, predicated on fabrications and bad faith. The United States will not participate in or legitimize this charade. 

For all of these reasons, the United States will vote “no” on this resolution.

after.Brazil:
Brazil abstained in the voting on the draft resolution submitted by the Russian Federation.

Brazil attaches the utmost importance to the Biological and Toxin Weapons Convention (BTWC) as a cornerstone of the multilateral disarmament and non-proliferation architecture. The complete prohibition of the development, production, and stockpiling of biological and toxin weapons and their destruction is an essential objective for international peace and security.

We followed closely the formal consultative meeting convened under Article V of the Convention in Geneva this past September, where States Parties had the opportunity to present their views, pose questions, and provide clarifications regarding the concerns raised. We believe that consultations and cooperation among States Parties, strictly within the framework established by the Convention, remain the appropriate and most constructive avenue for resolving any questions regarding compliance.

While Article VI of the BTWC provides for the right of any State Party to lodge a complaint with the Security Council, any investigation initiated by the Council must be based on solid, credible, and objective technical grounds and should command the confidence of the international community.

Today’s discussion highlights once again the longstanding structural deficit of the BTWC, namely the absence of an independent, multilateral verification mechanism. Brazil has consistently advocated for the strengthening of the Convention, including through the resumption of negotiations on a legally binding protocol equipped with an effective, impartial, and non-discriminatory verification regime. 

With the Ninth Review Conference of the States Parties to the BTWC scheduled to take place in Geneva in just a few weeks, we urge all States Parties to engage constructively to revitalize and strengthen the institutional framework of the Convention, so that it can effectively address compliance issues, dispel doubts, and preserve its integrity.
after.China:
(spoke in Chinese): China has consistently stood for the complete prohibition and thorough destruction of all weapons of mass destruction, including biological and chemical weapons. We resolutely oppose the development, possession, or use of biological and chemical weapons by any country under any circumstances, and urge all countries that have not yet done so to destroy their stockpiles of such weapons as soon as possible.

The Biological Weapons Convention (BTWC) is the cornerstone of global biosecurity governance. All States parties should strictly comply with their obligations under the Convention, maintain its authority and effectiveness, and refrain from double standards.

China believes that any information or clue regarding non-compliance with the BTWC should be taken seriously and properly addressed by the international community. The Russian Federation has submitted complaints to the Security Council regarding the compliance of the United States and Ukraine with the Convention and requested the establishment of a commission of inquiry pursuant to Article VI of the Convention. Under Article VI of the BTWC, States parties have the right to lodge a complaint with the Security Council, and the Security Council has the responsibility to consider such complaints.

China participated in the Formal Consultative Meeting of the States Parties to the BTWC held in Geneva this past September. We note that during the consultative meeting, the questions and concerns raised by the relevant party were not fully clarified or resolved. When a State party raises questions about compliance, the relevant parties should adopt a responsible attitude, cooperate actively in providing clarifications, and accept verification, so as to dispel doubts and rebuild trust.

Initiating an investigation through the Security Council pursuant to Article VI is a legitimate right of States parties provided for by the Convention. China supports a fair, objective, and professional investigation into the relevant issues by the Council. Based on this principled position, China voted in favour of the draft resolution submitted by the Russian Federation.

Regrettably, the draft resolution was not adopted today. China hopes that all parties concerned will continue to handle this issue properly through dialogue and consultation under the framework of the BTWC.

I would also like to emphasize that the lack of a verification mechanism has long been a major shortcoming of the BTWC. China has consistently supported negotiations to establish a legally binding multilateral verification protocol with comprehensive, effective, and non-discriminatory verification measures, so as to comprehensively enhance the effectiveness and authority of the Convention. We call on all States parties to take the upcoming Ninth Review Conference as an opportunity to restart negotiations on a verification protocol as soon as possible and work together to safeguard global biological security.

I thank you, Mr. President.
after.France:
(spoke in French): France voted against the draft resolution submitted by the Russian Federation.

For months now, Russia has repeatedly sought to instrumentalize the Security Council as a platform for propaganda, recycling unfounded and irresponsible allegations regarding alleged military biological activities in Ukraine. We have said it time and again: these allegations have no basis in reality. The High Representative for Disarmament Affairs has repeatedly confirmed before this Council that the United Nations is not aware of any biological weapons programme in Ukraine.

Furthermore, a formal consultative meeting of States Parties under Article V of the Biological Weapons Convention was convened in Geneva in September. During that meeting, Ukraine and the United States provided comprehensive, transparent and scientifically sound answers to all of Russia's questions. The overwhelming majority of States Parties recognized this.

The draft resolution presented today was not a genuine initiative to uphold the integrity of the Biological Weapons Convention. It was nothing more than another attempt to legitimize baseless claims and to divert the international community’s attention away from Russia’s brutal war of aggression against Ukraine, launched in flagrant violation of the United Nations Charter, and from the continuous strikes targeting Ukrainian civilians and critical infrastructure.

France remains steadfastly committed to the Biological Weapons Convention, an essential pillar of the disarmament and non-proliferation architecture. We will continue to work constructively with all States Parties to strengthen the Convention, particularly in view of the upcoming Ninth Review Conference in Geneva, and we firmly reject any attempt to abuse its mechanisms for political and disinformation purposes.
after.India:
Mr. President,

India attaches high importance to the Biological and Toxin Weapons Convention (BTWC) as a key global and non-discriminatory disarmament convention, prohibiting an entire category of weapons of mass destruction. We underline the need to ensure the full and effective implementation of the Convention in letter and spirit.

We also reiterate the need to negotiate a comprehensive and legally binding protocol providing for an effective, universal, and non-discriminatory verification mechanism to strengthen the implementation of the BTWC. This is necessary to equip the Convention with the relevant tools to address non-compliance and verify implementation. We hope that the upcoming Ninth Review Conference of the BTWC to be held in Geneva later this month will provide a useful opportunity for States parties to review the operation of the Convention and consider ways and means to strengthen its implementation.

India considers that matters relating to obligations under the BTWC should be addressed in accordance with the provisions of the Convention and through consultation and cooperation among the parties concerned. India participated in the Article V consultative meeting held in Geneva in September this year. 

Bearing in mind the prevailing circumstances and our consistent position on this issue, India has abstained on the draft resolution.

I thank you, Mr. President.
after.Ireland:
Ireland abstained on the draft resolution presented today. 

Ireland attaches the utmost importance to the Biological and Toxin Weapons Convention (BTWC) as a fundamental pillar of the multilateral disarmament and non-proliferation architecture. We are fully committed to upholding its integrity and strengthening its implementation, particularly as we look ahead to the Ninth Review Conference in Geneva later this month.

The Convention contains established, dedicated mechanisms to address compliance concerns and resolve disputes. In September, a Formal Consultative Meeting was convened in Geneva under Article V of the Convention to examine the allegations raised by the Russian Federation. During that meeting, both Ukraine and the United States provided detailed, substantive, and transparent answers to the questions raised. Furthermore, the High Representative for Disarmament Affairs has repeatedly confirmed to this Council that the United Nations is not aware of any biological weapons programme in Ukraine.

Ireland has listened carefully to the discussions in Geneva and in this chamber. We have seen no credible or substantiated evidence to support the claims of non-compliance by Ukraine or the United States, nor to justify establishing a commission of inquiry under Article VI of the Convention. 

The Security Council must not be used as a platform for unfounded allegations, nor should the legitimate mechanisms of the BTWC be instrumentalised to distract from the reality of the Russian Federation’s unprovoked, unjustified, and illegal war of aggression against Ukraine. 

At the same time, Ireland has always supported the right of States Parties to invoke the provisions of the Convention, including Article VI. Our abstention today reflects our principled commitment to the framework of the BTWC and its multilateral processes, while rejecting the unsubstantiated claims before us. 

We urge all States Parties to engage constructively at the upcoming Review Conference to genuinely strengthen the BTWC and reinforce the global norm against biological weapons. Finally, Ireland reaffirms its steadfast commitment to the sovereignty, independence, and territorial integrity of Ukraine within its internationally recognised borders.
after.Mexico:
Mr. President,

Mexico abstained in the voting on the draft resolution presented by the Russian Federation, and I wish to briefly explain the reasons for our vote.

Mexico maintains an unwavering commitment to general and complete disarmament and the non-proliferation of all weapons of mass destruction. We strictly adhere to the Biological and Toxin Weapons Convention (BTWC), which represents a cornerstone of the international disarmament architecture.

Mexico has consistently lamented the absence of a multilateral verification mechanism within the Convention. This structural deficiency makes it difficult to objectively clarify allegations of non-compliance and assess compliance with its provisions. We believe that the upcoming Ninth Review Conference of the States Parties, to be held in Geneva, offers the appropriate multilateral framework to address these systemic challenges, strengthen the Convention, and work toward establishing an effective verification mechanism.

Regarding the specific proposal contained in the draft resolution to establish a commission composed of all members of the Security Council to investigate the allegations, Mexico believes that any investigation into potential non-compliance with the BTWC must be independent, objective, and strictly technical in nature. The Security Council is an inherently political body and lacks the technical expertise, capacity, and impartiality required to conduct an inquiry of such complexity and sensitivity. Creating an ad hoc investigative mechanism within the Council would risk further politicizing the work of the Convention.

For these reasons, Mexico abstained on the draft resolution. We reiterate our call on all States Parties to the BTWC to constructively engage in the Ninth Review Conference in order to strengthen the Convention and its institutional framework through the multilateral path.

I thank you, Mr. President.
after.Norway:
President,

Norway abstained on the draft resolution before us today.

Norway remains deeply committed to the Biological Weapons Convention, which is a cornerstone of the multilateral disarmament and non-proliferation architecture. 

The Russian Federation has repeatedly raised these allegations, both in this Council and within the framework of the Article V Formal Consultative Meeting in Geneva this past September. On multiple occasions, the High Representative for Disarmament Affairs has confirmed that the United Nations is not aware of any biological weapons programmes in Ukraine. 

Throughout this process, the Russian Federation has failed to provide any credible, verifiable evidence to substantiate its claims. The mechanisms of the Convention, including under Article VI, are serious tools designed to uphold compliance and address genuine threats. They should not be triggered on the basis of unsubstantiated accusations.

We are deeply concerned by the continued misuse of the Biological Weapons Convention and the Security Council to disseminate disinformation and to divert attention from Russia’s unprovoked, illegal war of aggression against Ukraine. Furthermore, legitimate international cooperation and capacity-building for peaceful biological and public health research, consistent with Article X of the Convention, must not be undermined.

With the Ninth Review Conference of the Convention approaching, our collective efforts should be directed towards strengthening the BWC and enhancing its verification and implementation mechanisms, rather than eroding trust through politicized maneuvers.

Finally, we reiterate our call on the Russian Federation to respect Ukraine’s sovereignty and territorial integrity within its internationally recognized borders and to immediately withdraw all of its forces from the territory of Ukraine.

Thank you.
after.Russian Federation:
Mr. Polyanskiy (Russian Federation) (spoke in Russian): 

We deeply regret that the Security Council was not able to adopt the draft resolution we submitted today to establish a commission to investigate the military-biological activities on the territory of Ukraine. 

The results of the vote speak for themselves. The Western trio of delegations—the United States, the United Kingdom, and France—along with their allies, did everything possible to torpedo our initiative and prevent an objective, independent investigation by the Security Council. This once again demonstrates that the Western States are simply terrified that an impartial commission consisting of all members of the Council would establish the truth and expose the facts that they are so desperately trying to conceal from the international community.

Regardless of the outcome of today’s vote, the legitimate and legally substantiated questions that the Russian Federation raised in its complaint under Article VI of the Biological and Toxin Weapons Convention remain unanswered. Neither Washington nor Kyiv has provided any credible or substantive explanations regarding the dangerous activities conducted in Ukrainian biological laboratories with direct military and financial backing from the United States Department of Defense. 

We will not drop this matter. We intend to revisit the entire scope of these issues during the upcoming Ninth Review Conference of the States Parties to the BTWC in Geneva later this month. We will continue our efforts under the Convention and within international forums to ensure full transparency, accountability, and the strict implementation of all provisions of the BTWC.
after.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort:
The United Kingdom voted against this draft resolution because Russia’s allegations have no basis in fact. Russia has failed to provide any credible evidence to support its claims.

Since the start of its unprovoked, illegal, and premeditated invasion of Ukraine, Russia has repeatedly used this Council to spread disinformation. Today’s draft resolution is simply another chapter in that campaign.

Russia already brought these very allegations to the Formal Consultative Meeting under Article V of the Biological and Toxin Weapons Convention (BTWC) in Geneva in September. At that meeting, both Ukraine and the United States provided exhaustive, scientifically grounded, and transparent answers that thoroughly refuted Russia’s claims. The vast majority of States Parties present recognized that the cooperation between Ukraine and the United States was entirely peaceful, legitimate public health assistance and biological research, fully compliant with the Convention.

Furthermore, the United Nations High Representative for Disarmament Affairs has repeatedly confirmed to this Council that the UN is not aware of any biological weapons programmes in Ukraine.

Russia’s complaint under Article VI is therefore an abuse of the mechanisms of the BTWC and a cynical waste of the Council’s time and resources. It was designed purely to distract the international community from the atrocities, missile strikes, and suffering Russia is inflicting daily on the people and critical infrastructure of Ukraine.

The Council has rightly rejected this draft resolution. The United Kingdom remains steadfast in its support for the Biological and Toxin Weapons Convention and looks forward to working constructively with all States Parties at the upcoming Ninth Review Conference in Geneva to strengthen the treaty, rather than undermine it for political propaganda.
